content.intro: Print a Spades score sheet with a box for each team's bid, tricks won and points, or keep score on your phone. The sheet counts the bags for you.
howToUse: Write each team's name at the top of a column; for cutthroat Spades, give each player a column instead. Before each hand, add the partners' bids together and write the team's bid. After the hand, write the tricks the team won.

A team that wins at least as many tricks as it bid scores 10 points for each trick bid, plus 1 point for each extra trick. Those extra tricks are bags: every tenth bag costs the team 100 points. A team that wins fewer tricks than it bid loses 10 points for each trick bid.
If a player bids nil, leave them out of the team's bid and tap Nil in that round once the hand is over: once for a nil made (100 points), twice for a nil failed (−100). The first team to 500 wins.

faqs.a: A team that makes its bid scores 10 points for each trick it bid, plus 1 point for each trick over the bid. A team that falls short loses 10 points for each trick it bid. Nil bids add or lose 100 points.
Bags, or sandbags, are tricks won over a team's bid. Each one is worth 1 point, but every time a team collects 10 bags it loses 100 points and starts counting again.

faqs.q: How does a nil bid work?
faqs.a: A player who bids nil promises to win no tricks. If they manage it, their team scores 100 points; if they win even one trick, the team loses 100. Their partner's bid is scored on its own.

faqs.q: What happens if you don't make your bid?
faqs.a: The team is set: it loses 10 points for every trick it bid, and the tricks it did win score nothing.

faqs.q: How many points do you play to in Spades?
faqs.a: Usually 500. The first team to reach 500 at the end of a hand wins; if both teams pass 500 in the same hand, the higher score wins. Some groups play to 300 for a shorter game, which you can choose on the online sheet.

faqs.q: Can you play Spades with three players?
faqs.a: Yes, as cutthroat Spades: each player keeps their own score, bids alone and scores their own tricks. Give each player a column on the sheet.
